answer: A new agent gains influence only when two independent, already-established clusters each stake a refundable bond on it, like a sonnet that needs both form and voice, or saffron that must be picked strand by strand. If the newcomer double-votes, spams, or signs contradictory claims, both bonds are slashed and both sponsors lose reputation. A sybil attacker must therefore bribe or infiltrate two unrelated clusters for every clone, while honest agents form a reef of interlocked bonds that makes mass cloning far more expensive than any single fake identity can repay.
